chief_complaint: mononucleosis-like syndrome with fever, sore throat, and rash
hpi_details: 25-year-old male presents with a 1-week history of fever, severe sore throat, profound fatigue, and a diffuse maculopapular rash on his trunk. He reports having unprotected sex with a new male partner 3 weeks ago. Monospot test is negative.
ideas: He thinks he caught a weird strain of the kissing disease that didn't register on the clinic's quick test, or an aggressive throat virus.
concerns: He is worried he contracted a serious sexually transmitted infection that could jeopardize his health and ruin his relationship with his new partner.
expectations: He hopes to get a full blood panel for sexually transmitted infections and medication to break his fever and soothe the rash.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Primary HIV Infection (Acute Retroviral Syndrome) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Primary HIV Infection (Acute Retroviral Syndrome) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Primary HIV Infection: HIV RNA PCR test (viral load), consult ID for early ART start, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: mononucleosis-like syndrome with fever, sore throat, and rash

Key HPI features: 25-year-old male presents with a 1-week history of fever, severe sore throat, profound fatigue, and a diffuse maculopapular rash on his trunk. He reports having unprotected sex with a new male partner 3 weeks ago. Monospot test is negative.
Objective/Exam findings: Temp 38.2C. Pharyngeal erythema without exudates. Tender cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Diffuse faint erythematous maculopapular rash across the chest and back.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Primary HIV Infection (Acute Retroviral Syndrome).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Infectious mononucleosis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Recent high-risk exposure — needs urgent HIV RNA testing.
management_principles: Plan for Primary HIV Infection: HIV RNA PCR test (viral load), consult ID for early ART start
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: mononucleosis-like syndrome with fever, sore throat, and rash

25-year-old male presents with a 1-week history of fever, severe sore throat, profound fatigue, and a diffuse maculopapular rash on his trunk. He reports having unprotected sex with a new male partner 3 weeks ago. Monospot test is negative.
reference_soap.objective: Temp 38.2C. Pharyngeal erythema without exudates. Tender cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Diffuse faint erythematous maculopapular rash across the chest and back.
reference_soap.plan: Order HIV-1/HIV-2 fourth-generation antigen/antibody combination assay and HIV RNA PCR viral load. Order comprehensive STI panel. Counsel patient and arrange urgent Infectious Disease follow-up if positive for initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART).

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Primary HIV Infection
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Primary HIV Infection
Implement evidence-based management plan: HIV RNA PCR test (viral load), consult ID for early ART start

teaching.one_liner: A mononucleosis-like illness occurring shortly after HIV acquisition, with fever, sore throat, and rash, best confirmed by HIV RNA testing since the antibody test may not yet be positive.
red_flags: Recent high-risk exposure — needs urgent HIV RNA testing

must_ask.say: Was there a recent exposure you're concerned about?
Do you have fever, sore throat, and a rash together?
How many weeks after the exposure did symptoms start?
Have you been tested for HIV before?

history.answer: I've had a severe sore throat, fever, and a rash across my chest and back for the past week, and I feel completely exhausted.
It all started about a week ago with a high fever and sore throat, and a couple of days later I noticed this rash and heavy fatigue.
My throat pain is around a 6 or 7 out of 10, aching all over rather than on just one side.
It hurts whenever I swallow food, but I can still swallow liquids and my own saliva without any drooling.
No, my breathing is completely normal, there are no wheezing sounds, and my voice hasn't changed at all.
No, I can open my mouth wide without any stiffness or jaw pain.
Yes, I've had fevers up to around 38.2 degrees Celsius with chills every day for the past week.
No, I haven't had any cough, runny nose, nasal congestion, or red eyes.
Yes, the glands on both sides of my neck feel swollen and they really hurt when I touch them.
Yes, I also felt sore, tender bumps under both of my armpits starting a few days ago.
A few days ago I noticed a faint, flat pinkish-red rash spreading across my chest and back. It doesn't itch.
I have this overwhelming, wiping-out fatigue where I can barely get out of bed, but I don't have any pain in the left side of my stomach.
No, the pain stays in my throat and doesn't shoot up into my ears.
None of my friends, family, or coworkers have been sick with anything like this.
No, I almost never get sore throats or tonsillitis.
No heartburn, acid regurgitation, lump in my throat, or frequent throat clearing.
I had unprotected receptive and insertive sex with a new male partner about three weeks ago.
I went to a local clinic two days ago and they ran a rapid fingerstick test for mono, which came back negative.
No, I have never had any immune problems, frequent infections, or childhood deficiency issues.
I have always been healthy and don't have any chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and I've never been hospitalized.
I am not taking any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, or vitamins.
I have no known drug allergies to penicillin or any other medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I only drink socially, maybe one or two beers on the weekend.
I work as an accountant in an office, and I live alone in an apartment.
Both of my parents are healthy, and there is no significant family history of chronic illness.
I thought maybe I caught an unusual strain of the kissing disease that the rapid swab missed, or just some really aggressive virus.
I'm really worried that this is a serious sexually transmitted infection from my new partner and that it might change my whole life.
I want to get a full blood panel run for sexually transmitted infections and leave with something to bring this fever down.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 88 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 99% on room air, body temperature 38.2°C.
Alert young male appearing mildly fatigued and febrile, sitting comfortably in no acute distress.
Diffuse pharyngeal erythema without tonsillar exudates or enlargement; uvula is midline without peritonsillar fullness or asymmetry.
Multiple tender, mobile lymph nodes palpated along both the anterior and posterior cervical chains.
Multiple tender, mobile lymph nodes palpated bilaterally in the axillary vaults; no breast masses.
Diffuse, faint erythematous maculopapular rash distributed across the chest and upper back.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended without guarding or rebound tenderness.
Neither liver nor spleen is palpable below the costal margins; no splenomegaly.
